definition: LocalCausalPrinciple supplies a distinct existing causal predecessor to each existing contingent individual, at each world. It omits a sufficient reason for the whole series and any regress-termination principle. This is a deliberately stated test premise, not an endorsed universal metaphysical axiom.
note: Analyst’s explicit reconstruction for the Kant inquiry (#250), not an assertion that the surrogate exhausts the historical concept. Source fidelity and the missing philosophical bridges are discussed in docs/kant-cosmological-inference.md.
